Name: Sara Stone
Question: What would you do if you found out your spouse was hoarding $20k that you didn’t know about? And during that time, whenever you asked for child care help or anything else that could give you relief because you were depressed, he claimed he had no $?
Answer: PRAISE, PRAISE, PRAISE, PRAISE THIS SPOUSE for being so SMART, disciplined, self-sacrificing and for not letting you break down their commitment to a very decent, loving, incredibly helpful thing to do. That’s not HOARDING; that’s SAVING. Considering what Co-Vid 19 brings up, in terms of what could happen depending on various scenarios… earthquakes, economic setbacks, volcanic explosions, farm productivity going down and food supply decreasing or food prices skyrocketing… your spouse is the smartest person in the whole wide world.

Question: What is the biggest way that churches water down God’s word?
Answer: The biggest way churches water down God’s word is to say that we’re not all supposed to walk in supernatural power consistently and on a daily basis. This is the worst kind of apostasy and makes the gospel of none effect because God is a POWER-filled God, and He has left us WITH the HOLY SPIRIT, and we have no excuse but sin and hanging back for not manifesting all the gifts and miracles that can come through our perfect union with Him.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How do you celebrate your birthday if you’re homeless with no "real friends" during a pandemic in a city on lockdown?
Answer: Be THANKFUL that you are yet alive. That you have been given the strength and tenacity to keep on keeping on even when everything is wrecked around you and to some extent inside you. Be CURIOUS about what the REST of your life will look like; whom will you meet? What is going to surprise you? What is around the corner? Be CONFIDENT that your story has not at all been fully revealed or told yet and that you are in a better position today, even in your situation, to write its next chapter than you were in December 2019 before the world’s economic and social landscapes changed so much. And, if you don’t have a problem with alcohol, go enjoy a nice brew on your special day and announce a toast to yourself in the fine establishment you choose to celebrate in. Happy Birthday! And don’t forget, there is no one else in the world quite like you and you have something special to offer; it just takes time and the right kind of efforts for it to manifest. Perhaps you can share a photo from your special day here soon!

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the most unbelievable thing you have ever heard preached during church?
Answer: I think the worst service to church attendees I have ever heard, and it still makes me just flutter my eyes at Fate’s cruel twists and turns, was the one at Chapel of Our Savior by Rev. Dayle Casey right after 9 - 11. Now, Father Casey is a diligent man, and known within his Episcopal denomination for his theology… his thinking about God stuff. The place was PACKED. Not a seat left open. Did that man in the pulpit talk about LOVE for Christ? Or Christ’s LOVE for us? NOOoooooooo! He talked about the misplaced loyalty of citizens towards their nations’ flags. Now, I am saying it far more simplistically than it was… for Father Casey is a thorough man with a broad reaching intellect, a good memory, and an abiding interest in things that make sense, but he wouldn’t fall into the category of ever just reaching PAST man’s corrupt mind, through the obstacles that surround his heart to that beating heart throb within that needs to know and be often reminded that God loves us, that we are to love God, and that we are to love others. He had a true treasure in his hand, to offer reconciliation to people who hadn’t been in church in a decade; to some who had NEVER ever gone before; to so many different kinds of people coming in or coming back for the first time… But he didn’t grab it. He pressed HIS work, HIS theology, HIS agenda and very few of those who were not regular attendees returned the next Sunday. Boy I would have handled that differently if I were in that pulpit that day. I wouldn’t have been talking theory, or good points of theology, I would have been talking to my fellow American about our need for one another, our need for God, our need to COME TOGETHER for many cooperative ventures, INCLUDING maintaining and growing our churches for the equipping of the saints and the succoring of those in trouble or in need. I was aghast. The deep needs that were in the hearts of people there, who needed, desperately to hear the Gospel in the simplest of forms and ways… but that is beyond many, not just the likes of the Reverend Casey.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What have you learned about your own mental health and that of others from the Covid 19 coronavirus pandemic?
Answer: I know what anxiety is now; I know how it builds up, how it ramps a person up, how hard it is to control when it is being caused by fear that’s just under the surface about something important that you have limited control over. I know some people don’t share their tensions or worries very often… they go it alone. I’ve relearned that getting out of the house and taking a walk, getting some fresh air, and OH NATURE, are all really good for a person, Co-Vid times or not. I learned some people (like President Trump) use denial REALLY REALLY WELL, but that in the case of Co-Vid 19, denial (of possible risk) is NOT good for the people around you. I’ve learned a lot about some of the specific ways in which our nation’s culture and political system is just junk; we are in far more trouble than I thought. The fragmentation of manners, the lack of facility with gathering knowledge, performing sensible analysis, then making cohesive summaries that hit on the important and don’t leave things up in the air in the readers’ minds, and the abandonment of just plain common sense is what characterizes America today. Whatever that horse was, the prized stallion, that kept us in the lead, he is so far out of the barn now, well, I don’t think we would recognize him if he trotted back in.
